requirements.evidence: Queue.php:25 defines DEFAULT_PREFIX_MAP and :37-51 implement prefixForPriority/defaultPrefixFor with the custom-map-then-range fallback; :27-32 normalizes on every save and :67-98 validates canonical keys, one-uppercase-letter values and effective uniqueness, returning null for an empty map. Ticket.php:38 changes nextCode to queue+prefix+issue_date with malformed/legacy codes skipped (:43-52), :140 casts issue_date to date, and :61-64 stores Y-m-d via an Attribute setter. IssueTicket.php:27 reads now() once and :46-58 use the same day for the code, issued_at and issue_date. TicketFactory.php:34/47/56-67 default issue_date from issued_at and allocate the code from the ticket priority and that day while keeping explicit codes. UpdateQueue.php:21/25-34/69-71 implement the nullable parameter, ValidationException mapping and clearing with []. Both migrations implement the requested up/down (055507:15, 055508:19-27).

conventions.evidence: UpdateQueue still authorizes via Gate before the write (UpdateQueue.php:23), the map stays out of Queue's #[Fillable] attribute, migrations use the generated stub shape and include down() (055507:22-27, 055508:35-42), all new public methods have PHPDoc, and docs/business-rules.md:107-118, docs/database-schema.md:101/117/156-159, docs/api/totem.md and CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] are updated. Deviation: the issue_date down() at 055508:35-42 can fail after it has already dropped the three-column unique index.

security.evidence: UpdateQueue.php:23 runs Gate::forUser($actor)->authorize('update', $queue) before validation or mutation, and UpdateQueuePrefixMapTest.php:76-91 proves employees/outsiders are denied; priority_prefix_map is excluded from Queue's fillable list, so it is not user-mass-assignable; Queue::normalizePrefixMap validates every key and value before persistence (Queue.php:76-94); no new Blade/Livewire or output/escaping surface was added; IssueTicket keeps using forceCreate for system fields (IssueTicket.php:52-59).

tests.evidence: IssueTicketPrefixTest.php:14-95 covers independent per-prefix sequences, range fallback, custom maps, daily restart, midnight and the single clock read; QueuePriorityPrefixTest.php:8-110 covers defaults, custom/complete/swapped maps, empty-to-null, non-fillability, invalid keys/values, effective uniqueness and revalidation on save; UpdateQueuePrefixMapTest.php:16-91 covers owner update, omitted/empty params, ValidationException and unauthorized owners/employees/outsiders; TicketFactoryPrefixTest.php covers issue_date defaults, priority/day allocation and explicit codes; TicketIssueDateMigrationTest.php covers backfill, NOT NULL and the new unique key.

simplicity.evidence: The implementation reuses Ticket::nextCode and a single Queue::normalizePrefixMap instead of adding services or new abstractions; the production change is small and localized to Queue/Ticket, IssueTicket, UpdateQueue, TicketFactory and two migrations, and it adds no speculative API.

readability.evidence: Methods are short and focused (Queue::prefixForPriority/defaultPrefixFor/normalizePrefixMap, Ticket::nextCode), names match the domain, docblocks explain the daily-sequence and storage-format decisions, and the error messages name the offending priority/prefix.

scope.evidence: The diff only touches the models, actions, factory, migrations, tests and the three requested docs (plus the matching totem API doc example); no UI, totem API code or unrelated refactors were introduced.

issues.explanation: down() drops the (queue_id, code, issue_date) unique index and then recreates (queue_id, code) before dropping issue_date; once the same code has been issued on two different days the recreate fails after the drop, leaving tickets without any uniqueness constraint, so it should detect that case and abort before mutating (or document the required cleanup).

issue_date is only derived from issued_at when it is null, so passing an explicit issue_date (or one that conflicts with issued_at) leaves the two fields misaligned, contrary to requirement 5's "must stay aligned with issued_at" invariant.

each factory-created ticket now performs an extra Queue::query()->findOrFail() lookup and throws for a queue_id that does not exist, where the previous path still allocated a code; using the already-resolved queue relation would avoid both costs.
the factory tests only exercise default prefixes, so the combination of a queue with a custom priority_prefix_map and factory auto-allocation (which must pick the custom letter) is not covered.

review.summary: The change adds priority-letter prefixes with per-queue overrides, daily per-queue/per-prefix sequences backed by tickets.issue_date, the issuance and factory updates, validation on save, UpdateQueue support and the requested documentation. The implementation and test coverage are strong and follow the project's action, authorization and migration conventions; the only substantive concern is that the issue_date migration's down() can fail midway on multi-day duplicate codes, with a few minor factory/test nits.
